title: Extending a prescribed projective immersion by admissible blowups
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, and let $f:X\to B$ be a separated finite-type morphism [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a quasi-compact open subspace and fix an immersion $a:U\to\mathbf P^n_B$ over $B$, for $n\geq0$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Open immersions and closed immersions of spaces are representable morphisms with those properties on every scheme test [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]; an immersion means a closed immersion followed by an open immersion. There exist a scheme $Z$, a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_B$, an open immersion $u:U\hookrightarrow Z$ with $i u=a$, a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ on the small etale site of $X$, a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ of the scheme $Z$ in the Zariski sense [pqf-def-coherent], a scheme $V$, and a commutative diagram over $B$ with maps
$$q:V=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X\longrightarrow X,\qquad b:Z'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}Z\longrightarrow Z,\qquad v:V\hookrightarrow Z'$$
such that $v$ is an open immersion, $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and $u^*\mathcal J=\mathcal O_U$. The morphism $q$ is representable and proper, and $q^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. Writing $s:U\to V$ for the inverse of $q^{-1}(U)\to U$ followed by the inclusion, the composite $b v s$ equals $u$. Here quasi-coherent modules use [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections, and the algebraic-space blowup is the relative Proj of the Rees algebra $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal I^d$: it is obtained by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. The scheme $Z'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}Z$ is the ordinary scheme blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] of the scheme $Z$ along $\mathcal J$, and $b$ is its structure morphism. No density of $U$ in $X$, Noetherianity, or reducedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 088R (lemma-blowup-to-find-embedding), with B a scheme. Blowup construction, affine chart representation, isomorphism off the center and properness: spaces-divisors.tex Tags 085Q (definition-blow-up), 085R (lemma-blowing-up-affine), 085T (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor), and 085Z (lemma-blowing-up-projective).

proof.text: Put $P=\mathbf P^n_B$. Its structure map is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence separated and quasi-compact. Since $B$ is qcqs, $P$ is qcqs: quasi-compactness follows from the definition of a quasi-compact map, and quasi-separatedness from [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] (a closed diagonal is quasi-compact). The immersion $a$ is representable, so testing against $P$ itself shows that $U$ is a scheme. The map $a$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. Take its scheme-theoretic image $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ and factor $u:U\to Z$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image, def-nagata-scheme-image-factor]. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], $u$ is an open immersion. The closed immersion $i$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], so $Z\to B$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition]. This proves the required initial factorization $iu=a$.

source.place: Tag 088R (lemma-blowup-to-find-embedding), first paragraph, form the projective scheme-theoretic image (scheme specialization of Tag 088G).

proof.text: The space $U$ is separated and of finite type over $B$. Indeed, separatedness restricts from $X$ to an open subspace by the diagonal definition. Local finite type restricts on etale charts, while $U\to B$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. Thus [lem-sfb-space-common-admissible-blowups] applies to $X_1=X$, $X_2=Z$ and their two identified copies of $U$. Write its blowups as $p:X_1\to X$ and $b_1:Z_1\to Z$, and its open embeddings as $X_1\hookrightarrow W$ and $Z_1\hookrightarrow W$. Their copies of $U$ agree. Here $W\to B$ is separated of finite type, and $W$ is qcqs by the same diagonal and quasi-compactness argument as in Step 1, using [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products]. The original $X$ and $Z$ are qcqs for the same reason. These hypotheses will be needed for boundary ideals and composition of blowups.

source.place: Tag 088R (lemma-blowup-to-find-embedding), second paragraph, common blowups from Tag 088Q; verify its finite-type hypotheses.

proof.text: Admissibility alone does not imply density of $U$ in $X_1$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qc-open-boundary-ideal] to the qcqs space $W$ and its quasi-compact open $U$: choose a finite-type ideal $\mathcal K$ cutting out exactly $W\setminus U$. Let $r:T=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}W\to W$. By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], $r$ is an isomorphism over $U$, and this copy of $U$ is schematically dense in $T$, since it is the complement of the exceptional Cartier divisor. Form the open subspaces $A=r^{-1}X_1$ and $D=r^{-1}Z_1$. By flat restriction in the same node these are respectively the blowups of $X_1$ and $Z_1$ in the restricted ideal. Restrictions of a finite local list of ideal generators remain finite local lists, so both ideals are of finite type and unit on $U$. Since $Z$ is a scheme, $Z_1$ and $D$ are schemes by the scheme clause of that node. Schematic density restricts to $A$: the injective sheaf map on $T$ stays injective upon restricting to this open.

source.place: Tag 088R (lemma-blowup-to-find-embedding), third paragraph, density assertion repaired by a common boundary blowup; spaces-limits Tag 0855 and spaces-divisors Tags 085T, 083S, 085S.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-compose-admissible-blowups] on $X$ to $A\to X_1\to X$, and on $Z$ to $D\to Z_1\to Z$. Step 2 gives the qcqs original spaces, and each centre is finite type and misses the same quasi-compact open $U$. Obtain finite-type ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and $\mathcal J_{\mathrm{et}}\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ restricting to the unit ideal on $U$, with identifications $A\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}X$ and $D\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_{\mathrm{et}}}Z$ over the original spaces and identical on $U$. The scheme clause of [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] gives a finite-type Zariski ideal $\mathcal J$ on $Z$ corresponding to $\mathcal J_{\mathrm{et}}$, and identifies $D$ with the ordinary scheme blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}Z$. In particular $u^*\mathcal J=\mathcal O_U$. Write $Z^{\prime}=D$ and $b:D\to Z$ for this map.

source.place: Tag 088R (lemma-blowup-to-find-embedding), third paragraph, retain the single-blowup formulation after boundary preparation; Tag 086C.

proof.text: The morphism $D\to Z$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties]. Since $Z\to B$ is proper by Step 1, [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition] gives properness of $D\to B$. The space $T$ is separated over $B$: its map to $W$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], and $W\to B$ is separated, so [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] applies. Therefore the open immersion $D\hookrightarrow T$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-cancellation]. It is consequently a closed immersion as well: on any scheme test its image is both open (the immersion property) and closed (universal closedness); the inclusion of a clopen subscheme is a closed immersion, since the structure sheaf map is a surjection onto the corresponding direct factor.

source.place: Tag 088R (lemma-blowup-to-find-embedding), fourth paragraph, properness makes the open image closed, Tag 04NX; explicit clopen verification.

proof.text: Pull back this closed immersion along $A\hookrightarrow T$. Its defining quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal O_A$ vanishes on $U$, because the two copies of $U$ in $T$ agree and lie in $D$. These assertions use the ideal/base-change/factorization clauses of [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence]. The injectivity $\mathcal O_A\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ from Step 3 forces $\mathcal H=0$: its inclusion into $\mathcal O_A$ has zero composite with that injective map. Hence $A\times_TD=A$ as closed subspaces, not merely on points. Its projection $A\times_TD\to D$ is the base change of the open immersion $A\to T$, so it identifies $A$ with an open subspace of $D$. Explicitly, on every scheme test this is the inverse-image open subscheme. Thus $A$ is a scheme; let $V=A$ and let $v:V\hookrightarrow Z^{\prime}=D$ be this open immersion.

source.place: Tag 088R (lemma-blowup-to-find-embedding), last sentence (small detail omitted): kill the pullback ideal using schematic density, then identify the open fibre product.

proof.text: Under Step 4, the map $q:V=A\to X$ is the blowup in $\mathcal I$. By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] it is representable and proper. Since $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, its inverse image of $U$ maps isomorphically to $U$. The inverse section $s:U\to V$ is the copy of $U$ already used in the common diagram: all blowup identifications restrict to the identity there. The two embeddings into $T$ agree on this copy, and all maps to $Z$ extend the original $u$, so $bvs=u$. Together with $iu=a$, these are every required equality; no density assumption on $U\subseteq X$ was used.

source.place: Tag 088R (lemma-blowup-to-find-embedding), final assembly and compatibility with the originally prescribed immersion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q117-bd2d49115 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 4 new nodes and every cited statement in full. The sources were Stacks 088Q/088R (spaces-more-morphisms.tex 9075-9223), 086B/086C (spaces-divisors.tex 4215-4260) and 0855 (spaces-limits.tex 3166-3215); I checked the tags in the tags file. In clones/live and side-live the item is still unsplit, its statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, and there is no re-split note. Source error confirmed: 088R's claim that U-admissible blowups make U schematically dense in X' fails for X = Spec k ⊔ Spec k with U the first component and the unit-ideal blowup. The repair stays on the source's route: blow up W in a finite-type K with |V(K)| = |W|∖|U| (0855), so U is dense as the complement of a Cartier divisor (085T/083S), then collapse the composites with 086C. Steps 1-7 close. Step 1: P is proper and qcqs, U is a scheme by representability, a is qc, u is open via lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image, and Z→B is proper. Step 2: U, X, Z and W are separated of finite type and qcqs. Steps 3-4: flat restriction to A and D, K is unit on the copy e1s1(U)=e2s2(U), and the Zariski ideal J comes from the scheme clause. Step 5: D→T is proper by cancellation (T is separated over B) and open, hence a closed immersion. Step 6: the ideal H of A×_T D satisfies H→j_*O_U = 0 by the factorization clause of ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence, and O_A→j_*O_U is injective, so H = 0 and A is open in D. Step 7: bvs = u. The new nodes are true and are not restatements: 088Q, 0855(2⇒3) with K|_U = O, the 084B/085Q-Z/083S blowup calculus, and 086C with explicit ideals. Edge cases checked: U = ∅, U = X, K = 0, K = O, nonreduced and non-Noetherian. A DAG scan found no existing algebraic-space blowup or boundary-ideal node; the existing ones are scheme-only. Batch-5: every listed trf or sfb citation is a general definition (algebraic space, quasi-coherent module, module functors), 03DX descent, existence of fibre products, or a generic qcqs/proper/separated permanence lemma. None is a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proof, so I accept all of them. I accept the tool_use lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper (generic properness of P(n;S)). Advisory only: chart-properties lists def-trf-space-etale-module-functors and lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers in stmt_deps but does not bracket them in its text.
